chunks: Ten - Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sayrafi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from Imran ibn Dhiyan, from Abu Tahya Hakim ibn Sa'd, who said: I heard Ali (peace be upon him) say:

Indeed, the companions of al-Qa'im will be young men; there will be no old men among them except like the kohl in the eye, or like the salt in the provisions, and the least part of the provisions is the salt.

key_terms.أَصْحَابُ الْقَائِمِ: Companions of al-Qa'im, referring to the early followers of the Mahdi
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: al-Qa'im (The Riser), a title for the Twelfth Imam in Shia eschatology
key_terms.زَادٍ: Provisions or supplies, metaphorically referring to the community or group
key_terms.شَبَابٌ: Young men, indicating the primary demographic of the companions
key_terms.كُحْلٌ: Kohl, used here as a metaphor for something small but distinctive or preserving

ai.seo_question: Who are the companions of al-Qa'im and what is the significance of their age?
ai.summary: In the tradition of al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) characterizes the army of al-Qa'im as predominantly youthful, with the few elders serving as vital stabilizers akin to 'salt in provisions.' This metaphor underscores the Shia eschatological view that while the movement is driven by the vigor of youth, the wisdom of the few elders ensures continuity and preservation, reflecting the dynamic balance between energy and experience in the final victory. The comparison highlights the essential yet minimal role of the elderly, emphasizing that the core strength lies in the youth, while the elders provide the necessary 'flavor' or stability to the collective effort.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (10) Ali bin al-Husayn narrated from Muhammad bin Yahya al-Attar from Muhammad bin Hassaan ar-Razi from Muhammad bin Ali as-Sayrafi from Abdurrahman bin Abu Hashim from Amr bin Abul Miqdam from Imran bin Dhabyan from Abu Yahya Hakeem bin Sa’d that Imam Ali (as) had said: “
The companions of al-Qa’im will be young men. There will be no old men among them except like the kohl in an eye or like the salt in the food and the least part of food is the salt.”
